## phenix settings db

View or edit legacy database settings

### Synopsis

```text
Manage legacy settings stored in the internal database. For active runtime configuration (logging, etc.), use the root settings commands (get/set).
```

```text
phenix settings db [flags]
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help   help for db
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix settings](settings.md) - View, list, or edit phenix system settings
* [phenix settings db edit](settings.md#phenix-settings-db-edit) - Edit a setting in the database
* [phenix settings db list](settings.md#phenix-settings-db-list) - List settings in the database

### Examples

## phenix settings get

Get configuration value(s)

### Synopsis

```text
Gets a configuration value from the runtime configuration. If no key is provided, returns all settings.
```

```text
phenix settings get [key] [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
phenix settings get
phenix settings get log.level
```

### Options

```text
  -f, --format string   Output format (table, json, yaml) (default "yaml")
  -h, --help            help for get
      --json            Output as JSON
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix settings](settings.md) - View, list, or edit phenix system settings

## phenix settings set

Set a configuration value

### Synopsis

```text
Sets a configuration value in the YAML config file phenix read, or, when it read none, in $HOME/.config/phenix/config.yaml (/etc/phenix/config.yaml as root), creating it. A flag or PHENIX_ environment variable for the key still overrides the file.
```

```text
phenix settings set <key> <value> [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
phenix settings set log.level debug
phenix settings set log.system.max-size 200
```

### Options

```text
  -h, --help   help for set
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix settings](settings.md) - View, list, or edit phenix system settings

## phenix settings unset

Unset configuration value(s)

### Synopsis

```text
Unsets a configuration value in the config file phenix read, so a PHENIX_ environment variable or the default applies. Use --all to reset all settings.
```

```text
phenix settings unset [key] [flags]
```

### Examples

```text
phenix settings unset log.level
phenix settings unset --all
```

### Options

```text
      --all    Unset all settings (delete configuration file)
  -h, --help   help for unset
```

### SEE ALSO

* [phenix settings](settings.md) - View, list, or edit phenix system settings
